scope: All 1,451 pinned ScholarQA-Bio question stems reviewed for scientific topics and possible quantitative components. Every complete synthesis endpoint remains unresolved and unassigned. Other domains and single-paper QA sets remain outside this inventory.

inventory_completeness.inspection: All IDs, question hashes and stems reviewed. Topic annotations identify source themes; per-ID component limits live in workflow_designs/scholarqabench-bio.json. No complete synthesis contract is established; source evidence and answers remain uninspected.

source_grading.inspection: Static source only; not executed. README lists long-form outputs and citation scoring for ScholarQA-Bio, with no answer-label availability indicated. Citation entailment uses a learned attribution model.
source_grading.no_judge_limit: Exact source linkage and numerical extraction can be verified deterministically on independently authored evidence, but do not establish open-ended synthesis correctness or citation entailment.

license_and_lineage: The source README gives ODC-BY for aggregate data and requires constituent-license review. No source question text, reference contexts, expected answers or biological fixtures are vendored here or cleared for training.

task_defaults.assessment: Identity and question hash enumerated. reviewed_scientific_topic marks inspected stems; per-ID component dispositions are in the linked design file. All complete synthesis contracts remain unresolved.

biomedical-literature-synthesis.scientific_decision: Retrieve and synthesize biomedical literature with source-grounded citations.
required_stages: resolve the scientific question and evidence scope
reconcile findings and uncertainty across sources
write a supported synthesis with citations
scientific_constraints: Retrieval success and citation existence do not establish scientific entailment.
An offline frozen corpus changes the retrieval boundary; disclose that adaptation.
remaining_gaps: Review the exact individual question before creating any proposed mapping.
Select independent evidence and bounded, complete, machine-verifiable outputs; retain unrestricted synthesis as an uncovered objective.
Do not use source expected answers or inspiring papers as training inputs.
